deficiencies.description: The rewrite removes the hedge “kind of” and therefore presents the two-type classification as categorical rather than approximate.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: that tumors kind of came in two types.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: that tumours came in two types.

deficiencies.description: The word “since” adds an explicit causal claim that the terminology remains in use because surgeons can determine whether a tumour is movable by touching it. The source places these observations together but does not explicitly state that causal relationship.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: And you'll hear this kind of terminology even now, where a surgeon can see just by holding or touching a tumor, whether or not it's movable or immovable.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: This terminology is still heard now, since a surgeon can tell just by holding or touching a tumour whether it is movable or immovable.

considerations.sourcePassage: Okay. So with these tools in hand, I think the important concept to try and get across is invasion and metastasis.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains invasion and metastasis as the important concepts; the omitted opening and references to the lecture are transitional remarks.

considerations.sourcePassage: Obviously, changes occur within tumor cells, and it was long ago noticed back in, I don't know, when surgery was first coming into its own as a discipline after anesthesia was invented or discovered,
considerations.reason: The substantive claims about changes within tumour cells and the historical context are retained. “Obviously”, “back in” and “I don't know” are filler or hesitation.

considerations.sourcePassage: What they termed the movable tumor. And a movable tumor is exactly like what it sounds. Surgeons would find that that tumor could move within the tissue or an immovable tumor.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the terms movable and immovable tumour and explains that a movable tumour could move within the tissue; the grammatical restructuring does not alter the content.

considerations.sourcePassage: And a movable tumor, it was generally well-contained and had a capsule around it, and you could literally lift it out of that capsule. It hadn't really spread, and these are considered benign tumors.
considerations.reason: All the stated characteristics are retained, including general containment, the capsule, removal from the capsule, lack of spread and classification as benign.

considerations.sourcePassage: Immovable tumors, on the other hand, grabbed hard onto the tissue that they were seated in.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves this observation with only grammatical and British-English changes.

considerations.sourcePassage: So when it becomes immovable, these malignant cells have spread or invaded into the adjacent tissue, into the adjacent stroma.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the condition of immovability and the spread or invasion of malignant cells into adjacent tissue and stroma.

considerations.sourcePassage: And so invasion can be seen down the microscope, and that's something that you'll come to appreciate in your practicals, but it can also be just felt by a surgeon.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains both means of detecting invasion. The omitted reference to what students will appreciate in practicals is a course-related remark.

considerations.sourcePassage: So when somebody presents with a lump or a primary tumor, there will be a biopsy to look and to see whether or not the tumor cells are contained or whether or not they're invading into the surrounding tissue.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the presentation with a lump or primary tumour, the biopsy and its purpose of determining containment or invasion.

considerations.sourcePassage: Right. So, what does that mean for the patient? Well, the invasion, and whether or not that's seen histologically is probably the most important prognostic or diagnostic factor for the clinician in telling the patient what may or may not happen in terms of the tumor.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the qualified claim about invasion and its histological detection being probably the most important prognostic or diagnostic factor. The omitted questions and discourse markers are rhetorical transitions.
